plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: Enormous, ruffled, fragrant blooms unfold in silky layers of blush, rose and cream. Each flower can look like a spun-sugar confection on a sturdy, glossy-leaved plant. These blooms are a late-spring showpiece in cottage gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer, typically May to June
plants.location: Temperate gardens of North America and Europe, native to northern China and Siberia
plants.funFact: Peonies are long-lived perennials. A single plant can flower for decades, and some are said to have thrived for 50 years or more in the same spot.

plants.name: Rosa canina
plants.description: Arching, thorny stems spill over hedgerows and woodland edges. They are covered in delicate, five-petaled flowers with a soft honeyed scent and a golden heart of stamens. In autumn the blooms give way to bright red hips.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer, peaking from late May to June
plants.location: Hedgerows and scrubland across the United Kingdom and Europe
plants.funFact: The vitamin C-rich hips were gathered in Britain during World War II to make rose-hip syrup, when imported citrus fruit was scarce.

plants.name: Telopea speciosissima
plants.description: A fiery crimson flower head the size of a fist rises from a ring of red bracts. The head is made of hundreds of tiny individual flowers and stands out against the dark bushland of the sandstone ridges around Sydney.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere, mainly September to November, so it is not in bloom on May 31
plants.location: Sydney region, New South Wales, Australia
plants.funFact: The waratah is the floral emblem of New South Wales. Its flowers produce abundant nectar that attracts honeyeater birds.
